firstPlayerRule: Shuffle the four numbered Turn Order cards and deal one face up to each player. Put each player’s pawn on the matching turn-order space. The player in the leftmost occupied position takes the first turn; the others follow track order rather than clockwise seating order.
clarifications: The rulebook recommends dealing the cards blindly because their backs differ.
The two- and three-player setup changes do not replace the turn-order card method.
Later rounds can reorganize turn order through spaces on the track.
interpretation: With fewer than four players, use the leftmost occupied turn-order position. This follows the track-order rule when some numbered spaces are empty.

internalEvidence: Complete original English PDF hosted by Hans im Glück. SHA-256 63ff49cc1732960b3d8f8e2d858d1197a8b1985aa81603b7da5f94e30582a312, 15203699 bytes. Codex visually inspected PDF page 3 (printed 4–5) setup steps 8–9; PDF page 8 (printed 14–15) explains that the turn-order track, not clockwise seating, sets player order; PDF page 11 (printed 20–21) lists two- and three-player changes without replacing that setup. Cover names Helmut Ohley and Leonhard Orgler. Source review packet: artifacts/pending-rules-followup-sep28/REVIEW.md. Exact BGG 144733 / Wikidata Q25386738 directory identity; not Ultimate Railroads. Excluded from the portable random mix because numbered components set the full turn order.
uncertainty: The printed setup illustration is for four players. The lower-player section changes other setup quantities but does not restate the turn-order deal.
This answer does not cover Ultimate Railroads or expansions.
